reviews.text:
Previously Free Features Now Fully Locked Behind Subscription. I originally downloaded Avrora a few years ago and used it occasionally for simple things like the breathing exercises and sleep sounds (rain, ambience, etc.). At the time, I remember being able to use parts of the app without paying, which made it easy to come back to whenever I needed something calming.

After not using the app for a while, I recently opened it again expecting the same experience, only to find that the entire app is now locked behind a subscription. There are currently no usable free features at all unless you pay $3.99 weekly or $69.99 annually.

That change was really disappointing. I actually liked the app and would have happily continued using the basic features I relied on before. However, locking everything behind a subscription makes the app inaccessible for people who only want occasional or minimal use.

It’s also a bit misleading that the App Store listing doesn’t clearly indicate the full subscription requirement upfront in the same way many apps do. You only discover the pricing structure once you’re inside the app or after digging through the detailed information.

I understand developers need to monetize their work, but removing all free functionality from an app that previously offered it feels like a step backward. Bringing back even a small selection of free features like basic breathing exercises or a few sleep sounds would make the app far more approachable and likely encourage more people to stay and consider subscribing.

Right now, it’s hard to recommend this app because you can’t even try the app before being asked to pay- which is completely absurd. 
Feels money grabbing AND misleading.

I’ve also noticed responses to similar reviews mentioning discounts or promotion codes. While that might help some users, it doesn’t really address the main issue: the app can’t be used at all without paying. Even a small selection of free features would make a big difference.

I understand that apps need to cover maintenance and development costs, but removing all free functionality from an app that previously offered it feels like a step backward. Bringing back a few basic options like breathing exercises or a limited number of sleep sounds would make the app much more approachable and easier to recommend.

My reccomended alternative apps that dont require subscription:
“Rest”
“SleepWell”
“TheGrove”

Call Apple if you want to get refunded.. I usually don’t write reviews for apps, but I felt the need to do so as I realized there would be many others who are going through what I went through.

Simply put, if you wanted to try out the app before paying $40+ dollars on this app but ended up paying, call Apple Support and ask for a refund.

I won’t comment on this app’s features and functions, but they surely do a terrible job of differentiating between subscription and payment. Basically, the reason why this app does not appear in the Subscription list on your phone is because you are not “subscribing” to the service but “purchasing” a plan.

So, if you purchased this app, thinking that you were only subscribing to its trial, don’t waste your time reaching out to SleepSci. Just call Apple and ask for a refund (of course, you’ll need to be eligible).

Stops randomly. So I got this during the free trial and it worked well. The breathing exercise then meditation then sleep sound helped me fall asleep quickly. It worked well enough during the free trial I bought into it for $40 thinking I had found a solution to my sleep issues or could at least track what was going on during the night. Then the problems began.... I get no recordings of any noise made during the night and I know there are noises, for instance the other night I was woke up by my dog standing beside the bed barking at my face wanting to go out. Of all things that should have been recorded but it was not. My more bothersome issue is that if I wake up during the night... to let the dog out... the app doesn’t think I’m going back to bed so the app stops tracking sleep and the alarm never goes off. It also seems to interfere with every other alarm clock I have on my phone so those no longer go off inside the time I have programmed that I want to sleep in this app. 

It also doesn’t appear in the Subscriptions section on my phone so I don’t know if I can assure myself that it won’t charge me again next year. Contacting their customer support has gotten no response. My next step will be to contact PayPal to block further charges and an official complaint to Apple. I have been left no choice. Very disappointing considering the great sleep I got during the free 3 day trial.
